answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because terrace only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, umber is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any zephyr approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
